sourcePolicy: All questions in this pack are Ready2Go original draft practice items unless an individual record states otherwise. No official JAMB past-question corpus is included. Human subject-matter and answer-key review is required before public release.

questions.question: The value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made is called…
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up.

questions.question: Other things being equal, a rise in the price of a normal good usually causes quantity demanded to…
questions.explanation: The law of demand describes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, other things equal.

questions.question: A sustained general rise in the price level is known as…
questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level.

questions.question: Which factor of production receives wages as its usual reward?
questions.explanation: Labour is commonly rewarded with wages or salaries.

questions.question: A tax charged directly on a person’s income is a…
questions.explanation: Personal income tax is a direct tax because it is levied directly on income.

questions.question: Scarcity exists because resources are limited relative to what?

options.A: The number of days in a week

questions.explanation: Limited resources cannot satisfy every want.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Opportunity cost is the value of what?
questions.explanation: Choosing one option means giving up the next best alternative.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded usually falls when what rises?

options.D: Number of buyers in all cases

questions.explanation: A higher price usually reduces quantity demanded, all else equal.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The law of supply usually predicts that a higher market price leads to what?

options.A: A higher quantity supplied, other things equal

questions.explanation: Higher prices tend to encourage producers to offer more.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Inflation is a sustained increase in what?

options.A: The physical size of all goods
options.B: The population of one village only
options.C: The exchange rate in every case

questions.explanation: Inflation measures persistent increases in the overall price level.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Gross domestic product measures the value of final goods and services produced where?

options.C: Within a country during a specified period

questions.explanation: GDP covers final production within a geographic economy.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Monetary policy in Nigeria is primarily conducted by which institution?
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria conducts monetary policy.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Government taxation and spending are central tools of what?
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy uses taxes and public expenditure.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A market with many sellers offering similar products and easy entry is closest to which model?
questions.explanation: Perfect competition assumes many buyers and sellers and low entry barriers.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand measures responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in what?
questions.explanation: Price elasticity compares percentage change in quantity demanded with percentage change in price.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A person without a job who is actively seeking and available for work is generally classified as what?
questions.explanation: Standard labour statistics require no job, availability and active search.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Comparative advantage depends on having a lower what?
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is based on lower opportunity cost.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A progressive tax takes a larger percentage of income as what rises?
questions.explanation: Progressive tax rates increase with taxable income.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Which function of money makes it possible to compare the prices of different goods?
questions.explanation: Money provides a common unit for stating value and prices.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Human development considers income alongside health and what?
questions.explanation: Human development frameworks commonly include health, education and living standards.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.
